nodes.description: External view function selectWinner(address[] users, uint256 salt) that derives a pseudo-random index from block values and returns the selected user address.
Calldata parameter 'users': array of candidate addresses provided by the caller; its length defines the winner index range.
Calldata parameter 'salt': caller-supplied value mixed into the keccak256 randomness computation.
Local variable 'size' holding users.length, used as the modulus of the winner index computation.
Local variable 'hash' holding the keccak256 digest of block/environment values and the salt.
Local variable 'winnerIndex' = uint256(hash) % size, used to index the users array for the returned winner.
block.timestamp: miner/validator-influenced value used as entropy input for the winner selection.

keccak256(abi.encode(address(this), block.number, block.timestamp, block.coinbase, block.gaslimit, block.difficulty, blockhash(block.number-5), size, salt)): predictable on-chain randomness derived from miner-controllable block fields.
uint256(hash) % size: modulo operation whose modulus is attacker-controlled and may be zero, reverting the call (division-by-zero / arithmetic edge case).

edges.reason: The function selectWinner declares and consumes the calldata parameter users.
The function selectWinner declares and consumes the calldata parameter salt.
users.length is assigned to the local variable size, controlling the selection range.
The caller-supplied salt is encoded into the keccak256 randomness computation.
block.timestamp is used as entropy for the winner hash, creating timestamp/block-value dependency and predictable randomness.
The keccak256 operation produces the digest stored in the local variable hash.
The local hash value is the dividend converted to uint256 for the modulo operation.
users.length (size) is the modulus; a zero-length array causes modulo-by-zero revert, an arithmetic edge case.
The modulo operation yields winnerIndex, later used to index users and return the winner.
Execution flow of selectWinner builds the guessable hash used as the pseudo-random source.
Execution flow of selectWinner performs the modulo that derives the winner index.

normalization_plan.reason: The users calldata parameter only exists to serve selectWinner; it is not a core node and should be absorbed into the function node.
salt is only used as an input to the keccak256 randomness operation and can be merged into that unsafe operation node.
size (users.length) is used exclusively as the modulus of the unsafe modulo operation and can be merged into it.
The local variable hash is the direct output of the unsafe keccak256 randomness operation and is redundant as a separate node.
winnerIndex is the direct result of the unsafe modulo operation and should be merged into that unsafe operation node.
